target.title: fix: check channel health after startup grace
target.body:
Closes #105668

## What Problem This Solves

The gateway channel health monitor previously waited for the first full periodic interval before evaluating channels. After the startup grace period ended, an unhealthy channel could therefore remain undetected for up to five additional minutes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Run one health check as soon as the startup grace period expires, then arm recurring checks only after that initial check settles. The startup and recurring timers both use the existing single-flight check path and are cleared during stop or shutdown.

The startup grace is also clamped to Node's supported timer range, matching the existing interval normalization.

## User Impact

Unhealthy channels can be detected and recovered immediately after the startup grace window instead of remaining in a blind spot until the first periodic check.

This PR is AI-assisted. I reviewed the implementation and understand the timer and lifecycle changes.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/channel-health-monitor.test.ts` — 45 tests passed.
- Focused `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` — passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` — passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:core:test` — passed.
- Project-local autoreview — clean; no accepted/actionable findings.
- Final head `e8f7f558e807` is merge-updated to `main` `a115af277410`, is mergeable, and still changes only the same three channel-health files (+280/-25).
- The [full final-head Actions suite](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29648794017) passed: all 30 aggregate CI jobs plus CodeQL, CodeQL Critical Quality, OpenGrep, Workflow Sanity, iOS Periphery, macOS Periphery, and Shared OpenClawKit Periphery.

Local validation used Node 24.14, slightly below the repository's Node 24.15 engine floor; CI remains the supported-version proof.

### Patch-identical real Gateway runtime proof

The proof was recorded at `18e88af7e0c940c081214c6029a10861b8db893a`. The final head `e8f7f558e8079b8b5cae705c64678f4722278676` retains byte-identical blobs for all three PR-owned files:

- `channel-health-monitor.ts`: `342faac80bfed78a798ac57506378a2c59c7acdd`
- `channel-health-monitor.test.ts`: `8d754b6f9923f82657c56948313bc34f2cceda71`
- `channel-health-monitor.integration.test.ts`: `5d83acf9b5af142ff73372613fef020b00dc8a15`

Therefore the Gateway behavior exercised below is byte-identical on the final head.

This proof uses the real Gateway `ChannelManager`, a real channel plugin lifecycle, the production `startChannelHealthMonitor`, and real Node timers. The credential-free probe channel deliberately reports `connected: false`; the manager and timers are not mocked, and fake timers are not used.

Exact-head CI job: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29393022289/job/87280517945

```text
health-monitor live proof {
  "startupGraceMs": 80,
  "firstCheckAtMs": 81,
  "recoveryStartedAtMs": 205,
  "recoveryStopDurationMs": 122,
  "maxConcurrentChannelRuns": 1,
  "checksAtShutdown": 1,
  "checksAfterThreeIntervals": 1,
  "startsAtShutdown": 2,
  "startsAfterThreeIntervals": 2
}
✓ src/gateway/channel-health-monitor.integration.test.ts (1 test) 453ms
```

Observed behavior:

- No evaluation occurred before the 80 ms startup grace; the unhealthy channel was evaluated at 81 ms.
- Recovery held the first channel stop open for 122 ms, and the maximum concurrent channel run count remained 1, proving that no overlapping restart occurred.
- After monitor shutdown, three additional 40 ms check intervals elapsed without another snapshot check or channel start.

The setup intentionally uses no provider credentials, private endpoints, or external network. It exercises the production Gateway channel manager and health monitor lifecycle in isolation.

Exact-head supporting checks:

- Test types: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29393022289/job/87280517720
- Lint and format: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29393022289/job/87280517598
